response: Inhaled steroids have been found to be more effective than cromones in preventing hospital admissions for asthma in children. According to a study comparing two provinces with different practices for maintenance medication of steady-state asthma, inhaled steroids showed better results in reducing hospital admission rates for asthma in children compared to cromones. This suggests that inhaled steroids may be a more effective treatment option for managing asthma in children and reducing the need for hospitalization.
